answers.a: Côte d’Ivoire is reforming civil-service training through a new national framework for continuing training. The reforms include a procedures manual clarifying how training is managed and the responsibilities of those involved; a National Training Plan (PNF) to coordinate training, identify ministries’ needs and support planning and decisions on skills development; and the operationalisation of ministerial and interministerial training bodies provided for under Decree No. 95-92 of 1 February 1995. Ministries and institutions are also working to strengthen their training-management capacity, including within human-resources directorates, through better staffing, management tools and expertise in training design, management and evaluation. Other measures are the reorganisation of the National School of Administration (ENA) under Decree No. 2023-766 of 28 September 2023, with expanded initial and continuing training and diploma or certificate programmes; the development of professional placements, including placements abroad for diplomacy students; and digitalisation to enable e-learning and reach officials posted outside Abidjan.

answers.a: For the tax administration’s HR service (DRHF), the documented challenges are a lack of staff with the skills and experience to manage human-capital risks; DGI managers who have not been trained to manage those risks; no documented formal processes, apart from staff evaluation, for identifying, assessing, prioritising and mitigating them; and a quarterly staff-rating system that the DRHF plans to replace with performance-based evaluation. These are documented HR-management constraints relevant to effective use of its HRMIS, not reported technical faults or demonstrated HRMIS data-quality failures. The evidence concerns the tax administration, not a government-wide HRMIS.
answers.q: La DRHF n’est pas encore en mesure de gérer efficacement les risques liés au capital humain. La gestion des risques liés au capital humain est un chantier en cours. À ce stade, aucun personnel disposant de compétences et d’expérience dans ce domaine n’est affecté á la DRHF. Les cadres de la DGI ne sont pas non plus formés á la gestion de ces risques. La DRHF prévoit de remplacer le système actuel de notation (trimestrielle) du personnel par un système d’évaluation basé sur les performances. À l’exception du système d’évaluation des agents et des cadres, aucun autre processus formel pour identifier, évaluer, hiérarchiser et atténuer les risques liés au capital humain n’est documenté.

answers.a: Côte d’Ivoire’s 2021–2024 reform agenda includes: (1) biometric enrolment of civil servants and state agents, including centralisation and deduplication of data, maintenance of a secure and reliable central database, and biometric attendance control; and (2) implementation of SIGFAE2 to replace SIGFAE Web with a unified SIGFAE system using a single database and upgraded, reinforced infrastructure.
answers.q:
FULL ENGLISH TRANSLATION: The use of biometrics aims to strengthen the security and reliability of the SIGFAE database. It has the advantage of effectively combating absenteeism in public services and reducing the loss of State financial resources, with a view to better control of the wage bill. The use of biometrics will essentially be based on biometric enrolment, data centralisation, deduplication, maintenance of a reliable and secure central database of State agents, and management of biometric attendance control.

Implementation of SIGFAE2 is one of the recommendations of the 2018 BNEDT evaluation. Its completion will make it possible to take a further step by eliminating the current SIGFAE Web application, which will no longer be useful, and replacing it with a single SIGFAE system, available on a single database and on new infrastructure that is more suitable, better sized, rehabilitated and reinforced.
